transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I guess I'm here because I've gotten so strict about cutting back how much I eat that I hardly feel like I'm taking in anything at all anymore. It has just gotten to a point where it feels really hard to manage.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if you're underweight or losing weight?

Yes, I'm absolutely terrified of gaining weight. Even if the scale goes up by half a pound, or if I just think about eating pizza from the break room, I get this panicky feeling. I worry that if I gain weight, everyone at the warehouse will see me as lazy and unprofessional.
Do you feel that your body looks heavier or fatter than it actually is, even when others might say you're thin?

Yes, absolutely. Even though people tell me I look tiny and my clothes are hanging off me, when I look in the mirror, all I can see is my stomach and thighs looking too big. It makes me feel like I'm not professional or good enough, so I feel like I have to stay as small as possible.

The patient exhibits a persistent fear of gaining weight, significant restriction of food intake, and a distorted body image—seeing themselves as heavier despite being underweight—which strongly aligns with F50.0 (anorexia nervosa). No additional symptoms suggest an alternative or co-occurring eating disorder.
